objectives: List the seven characteristics shared by all living things.
Explain each characteristic with an example from plants and animals.
Decide whether an object is living or non-living and justify the answer.
reviewNotes: Whether the syllabus lists seven or six characteristics (some books group nutrition and excretion differently) is to be checked.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Living organisms
blocks.md:
A **living organism** is a thing that carries out all the life processes. Biologists remember seven of them with the words **MRS GREN**:

- **M**ovement
- **R**espiration
- **S**ensitivity
- **G**rowth
- **R**eproduction
- **E**xcretion
- **N**utrition

blocks.caption: The seven characteristics of living things (MRS GREN).
blocks.alt: Seven rounded boxes, one for each life process: movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition, each with a short meaning.

blocks.title: What each word means
blocks.md:
- **Movement**: an action by an organism or part of it that changes its position or place. Most plants do not travel, but their stems and leaves move towards light.
- **Respiration**: chemical reactions in cells that release energy from food. It is *not* the same as breathing.
- **Sensitivity**: detecting stimuli (changes in the surroundings) and responding to them.
- **Growth**: a permanent increase in size and dry mass.

blocks.title: The rest of MRS GREN
blocks.md:
- **Reproduction**: producing new individuals of the same kind.
- **Excretion**: removal from the body of the waste products of metabolism (for example carbon dioxide and urea) and of substances in excess.
- **Nutrition**: taking in materials (food) for energy, growth and repair. Plants make their own food by photosynthesis; animals eat other organisms.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Plants *do* move (a sunflower head turns, the sensitive plant *Mimosa pudica* folds its leaves) and they *do* respond to stimuli.
- Breathing is only the movement of air in and out of the lungs; respiration happens in every living cell.
- Excretion is not egestion: faeces are undigested food that never entered the body cells.

blocks.title: Is it alive?
blocks.statement: A student says that a motorbike taxi (okada) is alive because it moves, uses petrol and gives out waste gases. Decide if she is right.
steps: List what the okada does: it moves, takes in fuel and releases exhaust gases.
Check the other characteristics: it does not grow, it cannot reproduce and it does not sense and respond by itself.
A living thing must show ALL seven characteristics; the engine only imitates a few of them.
blocks.answer: No. An okada is non-living because it does not grow, reproduce or show sensitivity.

blocks.title: Life processes in a cassava plant
blocks.statement: Name the life process shown by each observation: (a) leaves bend towards a window, (b) a stem becomes 20 cm taller in a month, (c) a cassava plant makes starch in its leaves in the sunlight.
steps: (a) A response to the stimulus of light: sensitivity (a growth movement).
(b) A permanent increase in size: growth.
(c) Making food from carbon dioxide and water using light energy: nutrition (photosynthesis).

items: Viruses show some life processes only inside a host cell; many textbooks discuss them as a borderline case.

blocks.title: Classification
blocks.md:
**Classification** is the sorting of organisms into groups according to the features they share. It makes the huge variety of life easier to study. The groups go from large to small: **kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species**.

A **species** is a group of organisms that can breed together and produce fertile offspring.

blocks.title: Five kingdoms
blocks.md:
- **Animals**: many cells without walls; feed on other organisms.
- **Plants**: many cells with cellulose walls and chloroplasts; make food by photosynthesis.
- **Fungi** (mushrooms, moulds, yeast): walls not made of cellulose; no chloroplasts; feed on dead or living matter.
- **Protoctista**: mostly single-celled organisms with a nucleus, such as *Amoeba* and *Plasmodium*.
- **Prokaryotae** (bacteria): no true nucleus; very small.

blocks.caption: The levels of classification from the largest group to the smallest.
blocks.alt: Seven boxes joined by arrows in the order kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

blocks.title: Vertebrate classes
blocks.md:
- **Fish**: gills, scales, fins; lay eggs in water; cold-blooded.
- **Amphibians**: moist skin, lungs and skin for gas exchange; eggs laid in water (frog).
- **Reptiles**: dry scaly skin, eggs with leathery shells laid on land (lizard, snake).
- **Birds**: feathers, beak, wings, hard-shelled eggs; warm-blooded.
- **Mammals**: hair or fur, mammary glands that produce milk, most give birth to live young; warm-blooded.

blocks.title: Arthropods
blocks.md:
Arthropods have a hard **exoskeleton** and jointed legs.

- **Insects**: 3 body parts, **6 legs**, one pair of antennae, usually wings (housefly, mosquito).
- **Arachnids**: 2 body parts, **8 legs**, no antennae (spider, tick).
- **Crustaceans**: many legs, two pairs of antennae (crab, shrimp).
- **Myriapods**: long body with many segments (centipede, millipede).

blocks.title: Scientific names
blocks.md: Each species has a two-part Latin name (**binomial system**): the **genus** (capital letter) then the **species** (small letter). In print it is in italics; written by hand it is underlined. Example: the human is *Homo sapiens*; the maize plant is *Zea mays*.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A spider is *not* an insect: it has 8 legs, not 6.
- A whale or a bat is a mammal, even though one lives in water and the other flies.
- In *Homo sapiens* only the genus starts with a capital letter.

blocks.title: Which class?
blocks.statement: An animal has feathers, a beak and lays hard-shelled eggs. Name its class and one more feature.
steps: Feathers are found only in birds.
Birds are warm-blooded and have wings (forelimbs adapted for flight in most species).

blocks.title: Insect or spider?
blocks.statement: A small animal has 8 legs and two body parts. Name the group and say why it is not an insect.
steps: Body parts: 2 (a head-and-chest part plus an abdomen); insects have 3.
No antennae are present, which fits arachnids.
blocks.answer: It is an arachnid (like a spider) because insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts.

lessons.title: Using keys to identify organisms
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Biology — Characteristics of living organisms; classification; keys (to be checked against the official syllabus)

lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Explain what a dichotomous key is.
Use a key to identify an organism.
Construct a simple dichotomous key for a set of organisms.
reviewNotes: The keys here are invented for teaching; the leaf descriptions of the trees are simplified and are not a real field key.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Dichotomous key
blocks.md: A **dichotomous key** is a series of paired statements. At each step you pick the statement that fits the specimen. It leads you either to another step or to the name of the organism. 'Dichotomous' means 'divided in two'.

blocks.title: How to build a key
blocks.md:
1. Choose a feature that clearly splits the group in two (yes/no, present/absent).
2. Write two statements, each leading to a name or to the next question.
3. Repeat with the remaining organisms until each has its own name.
4. Use features that can be seen, not size or colour, which vary.

blocks.caption: A branching key: each question has two answers.
blocks.alt: A tree diagram: the first question 'Has wings?' splits into yes and no; each branch asks about the number of legs and ends at insect, bird, spider or snail.

blocks.title: Pitfalls
blocks.md:
- Every step must have exactly two choices and they must exclude each other.
- Use *observable* features of the organism, not 'is small' or 'is dangerous'.
- Always end with a name; each organism must appear once.

blocks.title: Using a key
blocks.statement: Key: 1a Has legs - go to 2. 1b No legs - go to 4. 2a Six legs - insect. 2b More than six legs - go to 3. 3a Eight legs - spider. 3b More - crab. 4a Has a shell - snail. 4b No shell - earthworm. Identify an animal with 8 legs and no shell.
steps: The animal has legs, so choose 1a and go to 2.
It does not have six legs: 2b, go to 3.

blocks.title: Writing a key
blocks.statement: Make a key for a goat, a hen and a fish using one feature at each step.
steps: Choose a clear first feature: 1a Has feathers - hen. 1b No feathers - go to 2.
Second feature to separate goat and fish: 2a Has fur and four legs - goat. 2b Has fins and scales - fish.
Check: each animal appears once and each step has two exclusive choices.
blocks.answer: 1a feathers: hen; 1b no feathers: 2a fur and legs: goat; 2b fins and scales: fish.

exercises.prompt: A farmer in Bafoussam observes a tomato plant for three weeks.

parts.prompt: The plant gets taller each week. This is:
parts.explanation: A permanent increase in size is growth.

parts.prompt: The plant produces flowers and then fruits with seeds. This is:
parts.explanation: Seeds will give new plants of the same kind: reproduction.

parts.prompt: Give two ways in which the plant shows sensitivity.
parts.model: It grows towards light (phototropism) and its roots grow downwards in response to gravity (gravitropism).

exercises.prompt: Which pair are both characteristics of living things?
exercises.explanation: Growth and reproduction are two of the seven characteristics.

exercises.prompt: Removal of metabolic waste from the body is called:
exercises.explanation: Excretion removes the waste products of metabolism.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a stimulus?
exercises.explanation: A stimulus is a change in the environment; a response is the reaction to it.

exercises.prompt: Respiration is best described as:
choices: the release of energy from food in cells
exercises.explanation: Respiration releases energy in cells; breathing is a different process.

exercises.prompt: A permanent increase in size and dry mass is called:
exercises.explanation: That is the definition of growth.

exercises.prompt: Which organisms feed on dead matter and have no chloroplasts?
